$comment: VAPP-260 (Engine E0, epic VAPP-259, docs/spec/apps.md §13.1, §14): THE ENGINE'S OUTBOX IS O1's, NOT A COPY. The entry, the writes, the overlay, the replay, FIFO order, the outcomes, the prune and the pending label are `packages/domain-contract/fixtures/app-records.json` `outbox` (VAPP-235) exactly as written (`$ref`; the TS reference re-exports `@exp/domain-contract/app-records` `outbox*`, the Rust Engine replays the referenced section). What the Engine adds is WHEN it applies (`modeCases`, `outboxMode`): a host with a `sync` provider (providers.json: Exponential's SyncedRecordStore, Spezl's P2P space) queues every app write as an entry and flushes on lifecycle.json's `flush` effects; a host WITHOUT one (`local` identity, a SqliteRecordStore: the softcoded app, eDE Local desktops, exported apps) has no outbox: a write applies to the store at once, in one transaction per call (a batch stays all or nothing), the store's own `writeId` dedupe still applies, and the pending label never shows. The record store is the authority in local mode; there is nothing to reconcile. THE ACCOUNT'S QUEUE (`syncedCases`, `SyncedRecordStore`, VAPP-272): Exponential's hosts keep ONE outbox per account, across its apps, persisted in the host's own store through an `OutboxLog` (`entries`, `push`, `ack`, `remove`: desktop sync sqlite, GRDB, Room), so the queue itself lives in the Engine once and each host only fills in the log and the transport. A case starts from the `log`, then runs `steps` in order: `submit` a host call's `entry` (`online` = the device's connection), `flush`, `rows` (the synced rows of an `app`, which prune its acked entries) or `prune` at `now`. `transport` scripts each write id's replays in order (`{ok: true, answer}` | `{transport: true}` | `{code, message?, invalid?}`; none left = no network). SUBMIT persists the entry first, then: with nothing else pending on a connected device it replays at once and answers its OWN entry's first outcome (`{done: <the server's answer>}`, `{refused: {message, invalid}}`, or `{queued: true}` on a retry or a drop); otherwise `{queued: true}` with nothing sent, and the host starts the flush. FLUSH: one at a time per account, FIFO across the account's apps, and a retry stops it. A refusal nobody awaits goes to the listener (`refused`: the failed-action toast); an awaited one does not. `sent` = the replays in order, `refused` = `{writeId, verb, message}` of the unawaited ones, `logAfter` = the entries left as `{writeId, state}`. The entries are re-read from the log only when the store is created (a restart).

syncedCases.name: alone and online: the call answers the server's own answer
offline: queued, nothing sent, then the flush replays it
behind a pending entry: queued, and FIFO across the account's apps
a transport failure stops the flush and nothing overtakes it; the next flush goes on
a retry on the call's own entry answers from the entry and keeps it pending
an awaited refusal fails the call, leaves the log and raises no toast
a later refusal goes to the listener and the flush goes on
NOT_FOUND on a single update drops silently (delete wins), and the call answers from its entry
a restart reads the log: acked entries stay, pending ones replay
rows that reflect an acked entry prune it; rows that do not keep it
an app whose rows are unknown keeps its acked entries; past the grace with rows known they leave
